_meta.description: AD&D 2E campaign-compatible random character naming tables. Campaign entries are drawn from supplied project documents; historical entries are generic medieval titles; generated entries are original fantasy-style material and are not claimed as AD&D/Forgotten Realms canon.
_meta.sourcePolicy: Use sourceType to distinguish campaign material from historical terminology and generated material.
titleEligibilityNotes: minLevel and recommendedMinLevel are generator plausibility gates, not AD&D 2nd Edition rules unless a campaign source explicitly says otherwise.
mode=class means the title should normally require one of the listed classes/classGroups.
mode=affinity means listed classes/groups should be favored, but the title can be allowed outside them if desired.
mode=social means the title is rank/status and should not be treated as a class feature.
mode=achievement means the title is earned by deed or appointment; listed classes/groups are only a default generation filter.
weight is a relative random-selection weight within the eligible title pool.
_meta.notes: Class vocabulary now mirrors the application's CLASS_CATEGORIES exactly, including the homebrew and generic entries. Removed 'specialist wizard', which the app never uses: both titles naming it meant any arcane caster and now use classGroups=['wizard']. Removed the psionicist group as unsupported, matching the half-orc treatment. Added classMatching and raceMatching rules, since both fields are free text in the app. Name and title records are unchanged from v4.

half-elf.note: Build the half-elf candidate pool from the union of human and elf entries, then add any explicitly half-elf campaign records. Do not manually duplicate ordinary human/elf names with half-elf tags.

unsupportedRaces.half-orc: Intentionally omitted from this dataset until the application itself supports half-orc character generation.

titleIntegration.note: The primary Name field may be used as an application key/export filename. Keep generated title/epithet separate from Name. If the app has no title field, omit titles from persisted character data or place them in non-keyed flavor/notes only.

_meta.titleChanceRule: Use the matching level band. Levels 21 and above use the final 70% band.

unsupportedClasses.psionicist: Intentionally omitted. The application's class vocabulary (CLASS_CATEGORIES) has no psionicist entry; re-add only when the app supports the class.

classMatching.sourceOfTruth: classGroups above mirrors the application's CLASS_CATEGORIES exactly. Keep them identical; a second vocabulary will drift.
rules: Strip a leading 'hb_' or 'hb-' homebrew prefix before matching.

A multi-class or dual-class character's class field holds a DISPLAY STRING such as 'Cleric 7 / Fighter 9'. Split on '/', strip trailing level digits, and match each part; the character is eligible for a title if ANY of his classes qualifies.
An unrecognised class matches no class or classGroup filter. Fall back to mode=open and mode=social titles rather than failing.
Normalise to one of supportedRaces before matching; the application does this with getRaceKey().
An unrecognised race should draw from the human pool rather than returning nothing.
